subject: Service impact: targeted regional disruption — immediate customer reroute guidance and follow-up
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-05T03:12:00Z
Subject: Alert: Elevated error rate in EU + APAC regions (first detection)

Team —

We are seeing a sharp increase in 5xx rates and connection timeouts for inference traffic originating from eu-west and apac-southeast regions starting ~02:45 UTC. Error spike is concentrated on our hosted routing path through provider X's metro clusters (eu-west-1b, apac-syd-2). Initial telemetry:

- 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% to 7.4% for the EU pool.
- APAC is reporting connection resets and TLS handshake timeouts; client retries trending up.
- No anomalous CPU/GPU utilization on our infra — appears to be external network/dependency saturation.

I attached a short CSV with span-level error counts and sample request IDs. There are multiple impacted accounts; SummitRetail is showing elevated error surfacing in their dashboards (ticket HS-987654).

Immediate ask: notify affected customers with clear reroute options (US fallback) and provide step-by-step instructions we can support. Karthik, can your team hold a rolling reroute (lb-level policy) and open a support bridge with the provider? Marcus/rachel please compile the list of high-visibility accounts and contact points.

Attachment: error-rate-eu-apac-20290805.csv

— Hannah
Senior Oncall, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-05T03:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Alert: Elevated error rate in EU + APAC regions (first detection)

Thanks Hannah — good catch.

Quick plan:
1) Notify impacted customers (summit, two mid-market customers, and Edge Cloud Ops partner) with a short, prescriptive reroute note and rollback instructions. Rachel, send the customer-facing note (template below) and include explicit API endpoint and DNS steps.
2) Karthik: initiate a temporary routing policy to prefer us-west endpoints for new requests from eu/apac where latency is acceptable. Avoid mass cache invalidation; preserve KV cache where possible.
3) Hannah/Marcus: open provider bridge, capture ETA for route restoration, and escalate to provider NOC.
4) I'll prepare a short post-incident FAQ and credit proposal.

I attached the reroute playbook (v1) — keep it tight: change region param on SDK (region=us-west), or update customer CNAME to point to us-west endpoint; DNS TTL guidance included.

I'll send the customer notice in the next 20 minutes.

Attachment: reroute-playbook-v1.pdf

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Luke Patterson <luke.p@summitretail.com>, support@summitretail.com, ops@edgecloudops.com
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-05T03:45:00Z
Subject: Important: Temporary routing guidance for impacted regions (EU & APAC) — action recommended now

Hi Luke / SummitRetail team,

We’re reaching out to notify you of a targeted network disruption affecting a subset of our hosted routing footprint in EU and APAC that began at ~02:45 UTC. Some inference requests from EU and APAC are failing or timing out. We know this impacts your user-facing flows and want to provide a short, supported mitigation you can apply immediately.

What we are doing now: we’ve opened an escalated bridge with the upstream provider and are steering new requests to our us-west pool as a fallback while the provider stabilizes affected metros.

Recommended customer actions (two options):

Option A — SDK region override (recommended if you control the client):
1) Set region override to us-west in your SDK/config (example): region = "us-west"
2) Keep current API keys — no rotation required.
3) Monitor errors for ~15–30 minutes; revert to normal once we confirm restore.

Option B — DNS CNAME switch (if you manage DNS):
1) Update your CNAME from api.redwood.example -> api.us-west.redwood.example.
2) Lower TTL to 60s for quick rollback; we’ll notify you when to switch back.

Notes and caveats: latency may increase by ~70–150ms for EU-origin traffic routed to US — we will continue to monitor and can apply targeted caching to reduce token costs. There is no change to data handling or storage — requests routed through us-west remain encrypted and logged under your tenancy.

If you want we can perform the override on your behalf for an agreed maintenance window; reply with approval and a contact number and we’ll start a brief runbook with you.

We’ll follow up with a post-incident update once the provider confirms restoration and we complete our internal analysis. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is impacting live traffic and appreciate your patience.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: reroute-playbook-v1.pdf
From: Luke Patterson <luke.p@summitretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: support@summitretail.com
Date: 2029-08-05T04:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Important: Temporary routing guidance for impacted regions (EU & APAC) — action recommended now

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads up and clear steps. A couple of quick questions from our side before we make the switch:

1) Data locality: our EU regulatory team wants confirmation that no persistent logs or backups will be mirrored to US-only storage for the duration of the reroute. Will the request payloads be temporarily processed in US but logs retained in EU?
2) Estimated window: any ETA from provider or expected duration?
3) If we approve Redwood to perform the override on our behalf, will there be any downtime during the switch?

We can approve Redwood to do the override if you can confirm (1) and (3). If possible, we’d also like a short run at low traffic first.

— Luke Patterson
Head of Platform, SummitRetail
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-05T19:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident notes & next steps — targeted EU/APAC routing disruption (summary for leadership)

Team —

Summary (short): provider upstream network saturation in eu-west/apac-syd caused increased connection failures for a subset of hosted routing. We executed a controlled mitigation (route new requests to us-west) at ~03:10 UTC which reduced customer-facing 5xx to baseline within 25 minutes. No GPU/host-level failure on Redwood.

Timeline highlights:
- 02:45 UTC — first customer errors observed (Hannah alert).
- 03:10 UTC — temporary us-west steering policy applied for new requests from eu/apac.
- 03:35 UTC — overall 5xx rate back to ~0.3% for impacted customers.
- 08:00 UTC — provider reports partial restoration; full stable lanes confirmed at 16:10 UTC after provider routing fixes.

Root cause (current): upstream provider experienced loss of peering capacity in two metros, leading to packet loss and TLS timeouts. We are awaiting the provider's final RCA.

Impact:~ six mid-market + two enterprise customers showed elevated errors; SummitRetail was highest-severity customer (HS-987654). Estimated touched requests: ~120k tokens worth of failed attempts across the window.

Customer commitments / follow-ups:
- We offered SummitRetail a transient service credit for the impacted window; Rachel please draft the credit letter and include an option for Redwood to perform the override for them next time with pre-approved contact.
- Provide finalized postmortem and provider RCA link by EOD tomorrow.
- Engineering: add a short-term automation to detect rising cross-region TLS handshakes failing and automatically trigger targeted steering. Karthik, estimate for that automation?

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20290805.md

Action items assigned:
- Rachel: credit letter + customer PM follow-up (due 2029-08-06 14:00 UTC).
- Karthik: post-incident mitigation automation estimate (due 2029-08-09).
- Hannah/Marcus: keep provider bridge open until provider RCA is attached to our postmortem.

Thanks all — solid execution. I’ll prepare an external postmortem we can share with impacted accounts once we receive the provider RCA.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
